findings.title: Exit code semantics changed for an already-shipped preview CLI tool
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the previously-unused value 4 is now repurposed for the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. The update-compatibility command (and its exit codes) were already documented/shipped as a preview feature before this PR. Any automation or CI scripts already built against the prior exit code (4 == recreate required) will now get a different, misleading result: exit code 4 now means 'feature disabled' instead of 'recreate needed', and exit code 3 now means what 4 used to mean. This silently changes the contract of a tool meant to be consumed by scripts/pipelines, which is explicitly called out in the docs as a GitOps-friendly, scriptable tool.

findings.title: New FEATURE_DISABLED exit code is not asserted
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the printed error message via cliResult.assertError(...) but never asserts cliResult.exitCode() == CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4). Since this PR also changes which numeric exit code is used for 'recreate' vs 'feature disabled' (3 vs 4), a future regression that swaps these codes again would not be caught by this test even though the exit code is the primary machine-readable contract of this command per the documentation.

findings.title: No negative test for rolling-updates feature being disabled on the operator
findings.body: The updated test only exercises the scenario where the 'rolling-updates' feature is enabled via FeatureSpec. The newly-added documentation (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc) explicitly states in a CAUTION block that 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' No test in this PR verifies that the Operator actually rejects/fails when update.strategy is configured but the feature is not enabled, so this documented behavior is unverified and could silently regress or never have been correctly implemented.
